newsitem.title: CONGO: Belgian defence minister visits troops in Congo.
newsitem.headline: Belgian defence minister visits troops in Congo.

text.p: Belgium's Defence Minister Jean-Pol Poncelet arrived in Congo to visit his country's troops standing by for possible evacuation of Belgians from civil war in neighbouring Zaire, witnesses said on Saturday.
Poncelet said on arrival on Friday that the 500 Belgian paratroopers were there on a "purely humanitarian" mission.

Opponents of Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko have consistently denounced any plans for the use of foreign forces in Zaire as a ploy to save Mobutu from rebels battling to end his 31-year rule.
Belgium has about 3,000 nationals in Zaire, its former colony previously known as Congo Leopoldville.
Poncelet was due to go on Saturday to Congo's oil capital Poite-Noire where part of the Belgian contingent is based.

The United States and France also sent troops to Congo last month as rebels seized key cities in east and southern Zaire, raising fears of trouble in the capital Kinshasa across the River Congo from Brazzaville. The three countries, operating separately, have a total of about 1,000 troops in Brazzaville.
The Western allies say their troops will cross the river into Kinshasa to evacuate foreigners only if necessary.
Rebels have captured more than a third of Zaire in the past six months, routing Mobutu's ragged army.
But they are still about 1,000 km (620 miles) from Kinshasa which has been tense but calm, with no reports of attacks on foreigners.
Zaire's warring parties met in South Africa on Saturday for their first direct talks on ending the conflict.
